label: Michael Gold
narrative: Gold sat on the NASA UAP Independent Study Team and then, on 13 November 2024, took the panel's findings into the House Oversight hearing room as a witness. His written testimony is the clearest official-adjacent articulation of the aviator problem as a stigma problem: 'the stigmatization of the UAP phenomena is so harmful. The stigma prevents scientific inquiry.' He named Alex Dietrich specifically, saying she 'was mocked by her colleagues' and that her incident 'went years without any investigation' - a serving officer's career cost, entered into the congressional record by a former NASA associate administrator. His recommendations were structural rather than speculative: NASA should sponsor symposia to combat stigma, review archival data with machine learning, contact international partners, work with the FAA to establish civilian pilot reporting procedures, and leverage the Aviation Safety Reporting System. He also praised Daniel Evans, the study team's designated federal officer, for working 'under difficult conditions' - the euphemism that documents the harassment the panel absorbed.
